cefrAlignment: Matches B1 (CEFR CV reading for orientation: can find and understand relevant information in everyday material such as timetables, price lists, forms and short official documents): short tables with notes and symbols, and a form compared with an email. The arithmetic (10–15% discounts, doubled fares) is suitable for B1.
examFidelity: Timetable, price-list and form-plus-email tasks match TOEIC Part 7 and TOEFL Read in Daily Life text types. The short-answer and form-completion word limits are applied correctly. I checked every table-based answer against the table data: the times, the 65- and 30-minute journeys, £11.70, £178.50 and £51.00 are all correct.
fixes: Learn text: changed 'Questions then check whether the details match' to 'Some questions…' (overstated a TOEIC format claim)
ex2: added accepted answers 'Business English course', 'Japanese course', '6 weeks'/'six weeks', 'your student card', '26th of October' and 'Oct 26'
ex3: moved the correct option in q1–q3; before this, all of the first five keys were in position B
openConcerns: The lesson has 4 exercises, the minimum for lessons 5–12. Its 27 items probably fill 25 minutes, but a fifth short task would make that safer.
learnerOutcome: A learner can read across rows and down columns, use symbols and notes to change an answer, calculate simple fares and discounts, and spot details that differ between a form and an email.
